newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ to punish DKB on Wednesday - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: BOJ to punish DKB on Wednesday - Jiji.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will announce penalties against Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB) on Wednesday which may include barring DKB from raising funds via the central bank's daily money market operations, Jiji news agency reported on Wednesday.

Quoting informed sources, Jiji said the BOJ is also considering conducting inspections on DKB every month as a punishment for its alleged role in a scandal over payoffs to "sokaiya" corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike.
DKB concealed its illegal loans to Koike during an inspection by the central bank in 1991, Jiji said.

DKB's former chairman was indicted last week for allegedly extending illegal loans to Koike, and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) filed a complaint with prosecutors against DKB for concealing those loans during inspections by the ministry in 1994.
On Monday, DKB was fined 500,000 yen by Tokyo Summary Court for hiding the loans from the MOF.

Koike had allegedly used the loans from DKB to buy shares in Nomura Securities Co Ltd, which were used to extort money from the brokerage by threatening to attend and disrupt its general shareholders' meetings.
Nomura, Japan's biggest brokerage, is suspected of giving profits to Koike through illegal stock trades.

More than a dozen people, including top executives from DKB and Nomura, have been arrested in the affair, which coincides with the start of "Big Bang" reforms aimed at introducing more competition and global standards into Japan's long-sheltered financial sector.
The MOF is expected to announce administrative penalties against Nomura and DKB on Wednesday, and Jiji said the BOJ punishment will follow the MOF's action.
